## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `28c6fc09b8538570dff8e5a10aaa13ee4ffbab3a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0125-release-approval-gate-replaces-the-typed-version.md + .github/workflows/release.yml, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs, scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs, scripts/release-publish.sh, scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs, .changeset/config.json, package.json (the `version` script), AGENTS.md (Prime Directive #15), docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, docs/releases-maintenance.md, packages/services/service-push/package.json, and the published `@changesets/cli@3.0.3` / `@changesets/apply-release-plan@8.1.1` / `@changesets/assemble-release-plan@7.0.0` sources (the versions `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins; read from the registry tarballs, nothing installed or run)

Independent full review of the ADR-0125 amendment on card #30590, ordered by the 2026-10-25 rule (substance against the code and the first consumer, by an agent other than the drafter). Read: ruling 6663894403 and the whole #29466 thread, cards #30590 (triage 6666636809, claim 6671491544, dev report 6671957724) and #30591, PR #30719 body and diff (`origin/main...28c6fc09`, one file, +63/−1), the code named in Scope at `origin/main` `badf24dffc`, the registry (`npm view`), and the head's check-runs. The dispatch order, the drafter's report and the seat's conclusions were read as claims, not as evidence; every judgment below is against the tree. Check-runs on the head: 46; at the first read three were still in progress (Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Test Core 1/8); at the second read, 2026-11-05T23:26Z, all 46 had completed with no failure (success or skipped); no review and no comment on the PR.

### ① Derived judgments

**Fidelity to ruling 6663894403 — every bound line is present, none is softened; four sentences decide what the ruling left open (named).**

| bound line of the ruling | where the record carries it | judgment |
|:--|:--|:--|
| B: stable releases stay as today — QA sweep, Version Packages PR, approval at `environment: release`, publish to `latest` | "What the ruling binds" 1; Status line; "How D1 to D6 read with it" D1 | present, unchanged in meaning |
| a maintainer-approved `next` snapshot from `main`, proposed daily, dispatch-only | line 2; Status line | present; "proposed daily is a cadence of proposals, not a trigger" is a correct reading of "dispatch-only" |
| requires the full battery green at that commit | line 3 ("at the commit it snapshots"); "What the lane must satisfy — The full-battery reading" | present in line 3; **the requirement paragraph then names the stable lane's reader, whose answer is "at or before" (④-a below)** |
| `changeset version --snapshot next` in the workspace only, never committed | line 4; "Workspace only" | present |
| `changeset publish --tag next --no-git-tag` | line 4 | present; both flags exist in `@changesets/cli@3.0.3` (`dist/index.mjs:62`: `--tag`, `--git-tag` default true, so `--no-git-tag` negates it) |
| held at `environment: release` like the stable publish | line 5; D2/D3 paragraph; Status line | present |
| pushes no tag, no GitHub Release, never touches the Version Packages PR, ⛔ never moves `latest` | line 6; Status line; "What stays forbidden" | present; **the guard the record names for the ⛔ does not cover a package's first publish (④ M1)** |
| app repos pin `next` when they need a fix now | line 7 | present |
| two-week trial, then the director reports usage on #29466 | line 8 | present; **"The trial starts at the first snapshot the lane publishes" is not in the ruling** (named below) |
| the maintainer's three answers: every publish stays the maintainer's act, snapshots included; stable channel unchanged, `next` on top; today's `release.yml` has only the version-commit push and the repair dispatch, D1 publishes the version commit only | "Why", second paragraph; D1 paragraph | present and true at `origin/main` (② below) |
| workload: two Tier H PRs; a dry run of `changeset version --snapshot` on the fixed group and its `workspace:*` ranges before the first real snapshot | Status of this amendment; "The dry run" | present; the record carries no package count (right: the group is 109, not the ruling's 69 — see ③) |

Sentences that decide something the ruling did not decide, all in the record's own voice rather than marked as this record's reading:

- bound line 8: "The trial starts at the first snapshot the lane publishes." The ruling fixes the length, not the start. The reading matches the seat's own Restart-when on #29466 (6664069140) and #30591's acceptance, so it is consistent with the execution record, but it is the seat's, not the maintainer's.
- D2/D3 paragraph: the snapshot lane "is removed in the same change that reverts D1 to a dispatch trigger." D3 (ADR:71-77) voids the record and reverts D1; what becomes of a dispatch-only lane whose own event is a barrier is a new decision. It is the conservative one (Prime Directive #15 lets the relay dispatch `release.yml`, AGENTS.md:315-316, so the event alone is not the barrier it was before #6170's relay stroke) and I would keep it, marked as this record's.
- "What the lane must satisfy — The full-battery reading": "read the way the stable lane's `full-battery` job reads it, against the snapshot's own commit" chooses the at-or-before reader for the ruling's "at that commit" (④-a).
- "What the lane must satisfy — The approval screen": the job name says `next` snapshot and names the `main` commit. A D2 extension, not a ruling line; right, and it should stay.

Nothing in the ruling is softened except as ④-a states; nothing material is added beyond the four sentences above. The "Why" section's numbers are the ruling card's (1,700 PRs a week measured as 1,776; 214 changesets at `b17dbcf2`; 18.2.0 at 2026-10-27T06:20Z) and the registry's (`next` 18.2.0, `latest` 18.3.0, re-read here at 2026-11-05T23:2xZ for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/cli`, identical). "18.3.0 published 2026-11-03T15:16Z" is `@objectstack/cli`'s time (15:16:56Z); the ruling's 15:15Z is `@objectstack/spec`'s (15:15:07Z); both true, and the CLI is the package D1 reads.

**Truth against the code at `origin/main` `badf24dffc` — every claim checked holds, with one wording inexactness.**

- "its only publish paths are the version-commit push and the repair dispatch": `release.yml:182-184` (`push: branches: [main]`), `:199-200` (`schedule`, bookkeeping only), `:208-227` (`workflow_dispatch` with `force` and `refresh_version_pr` only); the one publishing job's gate `:1608-1612` admits a push with `publish-pending`, or a non-refresh dispatch; `scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs:381-387` makes a dispatch pending exactly when the version is absent from npm. True.
- "D1 publishes the version commit only": `release.yml:1657` checks out `needs.release-integrity.outputs.version-commit`. True.
- "`schedule`, which `release.yml` already refuses as a publishing trigger because a scheduled run is queued rather than guaranteed and is disabled by inactivity": `release.yml:193-198`, verbatim in substance ("Scheduled runs are queued, not guaranteed … disables them entirely after 60 days … the publish lane must never be reachable from `schedule`"). True.
- "Prime Directive #15 reserves dispatching `release.yml` from every seat, the fleet-write relay's refresh stroke excepted": `AGENTS.md:315-316`. True. "approving a `release` environment deployment" is on the list: `AGENTS.md:317-318`; D6 adds it: ADR:93-95. True.
- "refused before any deployment is queued — the direction the stable lane's `full-battery` job already takes": `release.yml:1497-1551` (`full-battery` needs `release-integrity`, `:1520`; `publish` needs it, `:1568`; its `if:` opens with `success()`, `:1608-1609`; the comment `:1509-1513` says exactly this). True.
- "the stable lane's post-publish acts — the atomic tag push, the GitHub Releases, the ADR-0087 D4 asset, the dist-tag move up to `latest`": `scripts/release-publish.sh:98` (`changeset publish`) and `:112` (`git push origin --tags`, run from `pnpm run release`, `release.yml:1977`); `release.yml:2030-2036` (Releases), `:2038-2049` (ADR-0087 D4 asset), `:2067-2073` (`release-dist-tags.mjs --apply`). True.
- "`next` resolves to 18.2.0 — a stable version, which the stable lane's post-publish dist-tag step leaves alone by its own rule": `scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs:40-42` ("a tag on a STABLE version … is left alone … `latest` itself is never written"). True.
- "the eviction the 2026-09-29 amendment measured applies to it": ADR:137-142; `release.yml:1623-1637` (group `release-publish-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: false`). True.
- "exited by #24528": #24528 is "chore(release): exit Changesets pre mode (`next`)". True (card #30590's "retired by #26196" named the rc retirement; the record has the right one). No `.changeset/pre.json` at `origin/main`. True.
- `.changeset/config.json`: `fixed` is one group of 109 names (`:10-121`), equal to the 109 non-private manifests under the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` globs (131 manifests, 22 private); `privatePackages: { version: true, tag: false }` (`:127`); no `snapshot` key, so `changeset version --snapshot next` composes `0.0.0-next-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` (`assemble-release-plan` `dist/index.mjs:241-263`: base `0.0.0`, suffix `tag-datetime`) and the fixed constraint gives every non-skipped member the same version (`:197-210`). The record's "rewrites the fixed group" assumption holds. Inexactness, inherited from the ruling's wording: changesets does **not** rewrite `workspace:*` / `^` / `~` ranges at all (`apply-release-plan` `dist/index.mjs:178-181` skips them); `pnpm publish` substitutes the exact snapshot version at pack time. A dry run that reads workspace `package.json` files will show the ranges unchanged; the lane's dry run must read packed manifests. Observation for #30591, not a defect of the record.
- D4 "the snapshot lane never reads `force`": consistent with `release.yml:210-216` (`force` = finish a partial stable publish). True as a requirement; see ③ S1 for the converse the record omits.

**Not decided here** lists three items (runtime image, the proposal's form, the channel after the trial). Right: `release.yml:2079-2101` builds the image off either lane's `published` output, Prime Directive #15 lists "pushing a runtime image" as a release act, and the ruling names npm alone.

### ② Semver level

None. Docs-only diff: one file under `docs/adr/`, no package moves, no changeset owed (`skip-changeset` label; `Check Changeset` green). `Clause-②: no` on the PR body matches the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

The boundary this record draws is "the stable lane is untouched; the snapshot lane writes `next` and nothing else." I tried to cross it from the first consumer's side (#30591, built exactly as the record requires) and crossed it once for real and twice in shape.

**M1 (must-fix) — a package's first publish moves `latest`, the record's guard cannot see it, and the case is live today.** `@objectstack/service-push` is a public member of the fixed group (`.changeset/config.json:52`), at version 18.2.0 in `packages/services/service-push/package.json`, landed 2026-11-03T15:59Z in #29794 (commit `8aa2e915`), 43 minutes after 18.3.0 shipped; two pending changesets name it; `npm view @objectstack/service-push` answers E404 — it has never been published. The first snapshot cut from today's `main` is therefore its first publish. `changeset publish --tag next` includes it (`getPublishPlan.mjs:605-650`: `publishedState: "never"`, still planned) with tag `next` (`:599-603`: an explicit `--tag` always wins), so the publish *carries* `next`, and the record's guard — "Any publish from the snapshot lane that would carry a dist-tag other than `next` fails the job" — passes it. The registry then gives a package its `latest` on its first publish whatever tag the client sent: changesets' own pre-mode rule is built on that fact (`publish.mjs:19-24`: "packages that have not had normal releases … will be published to `latest`"; `getPublishPlan.mjs:627-631`, the `only-pre` state keyed on a `latest` tag that exists although every version is a prerelease). Outcome of the first run of #30591 as specified: `@objectstack/service-push@latest` = `0.0.0-next-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` until 18.4.0 ships — bound line 6's ⛔ broken on the very first snapshot, and the record's sentence "`latest` is written by the stable lane and by nothing else" false. Fix, one requirement in "What the lane must satisfy" and one clause in line 6's gloss: the snapshot lane never debuts a package — a member of the group with no version on npm is refused before anything is published, because a first publish takes `latest` whatever tag it carries; the stable lane debuts packages. With that sentence, the "made executable" claim becomes true; without it, the record promises what the lane it specifies cannot keep.

**S1 (should-fix) — the two uses of `workflow_dispatch` must be exclusive, and the record asserts it without requiring it.** Under D1 the record says the snapshot lane "never consults D1′'s `publish-pending`, never alters it, and cannot queue D1's publish job"; under D4 only the converse is required ("a dispatch that does not ask for a snapshot runs exactly as today"). At `origin/main`, every non-refresh dispatch runs `release-integrity` (`release.yml:959-961`), `stale-prompts` (`:1459-1461`), and — whenever main's version is absent from npm — `full-battery` and `publish` (`:1521-1525`, `:1608-1612`; `release-pending-publish.mjs:383`). A snapshot dispatched between a Version Packages merge and its approval would queue a second, dispatch-lane `Publish X to npm` prompt in `release-publish-main`; `sweep` never touches a dispatch run (`release-pending-publish.mjs:174-176`, `release.yml:1443-1445`), so after the push-lane prompt ships, that prompt holds the group and hides the next real one — the 17.4.0 shape the 2026-09-29 amendment measured (ADR:142), this time un-sweepable. Fix: add to "What the lane must satisfy" that a dispatch asking for a snapshot runs none of the stable lane's jobs (the snapshot input is read by `release-integrity`, `stale-prompts`, `full-battery` and `publish` exactly as `refresh_version_pr` is today — strictly subtractive, `release.yml:218-222`), and that the snapshot job runs on no other dispatch. The D5 paragraph's "the group spelling is the lane's" is fine; the exclusivity is the record's property and belongs in its list.

**S2 (should-fix) — `next` is already ADR-0087's pre-mode channel, and the record is silent on the collision.** ADR-0087:335: "Every major is published to the `next` dist-tag at least one RC cycle before"; `docs/releases-maintenance.md:191-201`: two channels, `next` = "the pre-release (X.Y.Z-next.N), published by `release.yml` in pre mode"; `release-dist-tags.mjs:43-47` says the same. While `.changeset/pre.json` says `mode: pre`, `changeset version --snapshot` is refused ("Snapshot release is not allowed in pre mode", `version.mjs:47-53`) and `changeset publish --tag` is refused ("Releasing under custom tag is not allowed in pre mode", `publish.mjs:61-66`): a snapshot approved during a major's RC cycle fails after approval and publishes nothing — loud, but a wasted approval and an unexplained red run in the maintainer's name. Fix: one sentence that the lane refuses (before any deployment is queued) while pre mode is on, because the major's RC cycle owns `next` under ADR-0087; and name `docs/releases-maintenance.md`'s channel table as a consumer #30591 updates (`next` gains a second publisher and a second version shape). One more consequence to state for the "App repositories pin `next`" line: at each stable publish `release-dist-tags.mjs:35-37` moves `next` up to the new stable (a `0.0.0-next-…` snapshot is a prerelease below every stable), so `next` = the stable version between a release and the following snapshot. Intended since #25581, consistent with "never moves `latest`", and the thing a `next` pinner will notice first.

**Smaller flags, none a finding on its own:**

- The fixed group is 109 packages, not the "69" the ruling and #30591 carry (that figure is the rc.3 / rc.4 count, ADR:73). The record carries no number — right. #30591 should correct its acceptance line.
- `scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs:282` reads any job named `Publish (one token) to npm (awaiting approval)` as a stable prompt; the snapshot job's name must not match that shape. A name with spaces in the middle ("Publish `next` snapshot of main@sha to npm") does not.
- Under `--snapshot` changesets still deletes the consumed changeset files from the checkout (`apply-release-plan` `dist/index.mjs:302-320`, not guarded by `snapshot`) and writes `CHANGELOG.md` entries through `scripts/changeset-changelog.mjs` (`:288-292`); `commit` is forced false (`version.mjs:38`). The record's "workspace only, never committed" covers it; the changelog generator's token need is the lane's.
- The ruling's bare `changeset version --snapshot next` is right and the lane must not substitute `pnpm run version`: that script (`package.json` `version`) runs `sync-protocol-version.mjs`, which refuses a major below 1 (`scripts/sync-protocol-version.mjs`, "cannot parse major", exit 1 when the parsed major is not an integer of 1 or more), and the template / docs-image / skill-compatibility syncs would pin the stable versions anyway. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays at the protocol major, which is correct for a snapshot.
- D3 paragraph wording: "a dispatch with no human behind the approval is the rc.3 / rc.4 shape under a different dist-tag" is inexact — rc.3 / rc.4 had no human anywhere in the trigger chain (ADR:73); a dispatch has one at the dispatch. The conclusion (void with the push lane) stands for the relay reason given in ①.

### ④ Design judgment

**The ADR against its first consumer (#30591) and the code it cites.** The record is well built: it restates the ruling line by line, reads D1 to D6 against the real `release.yml` accurately (every file:line in ② holds), separates requirements on the lane from workflow text, and lists what it does not decide. It fails on one point of substance — M1 — where the lane it specifies, built exactly as written and passing its own guard, moves `latest` on its first run because of a package that is in the tree today. That is the ruling's strongest line, the record claims the guard makes it executable, and the claim is false for a case the registry already presents. A one-sentence requirement repairs it; until it is there the record cannot be the thing #30591 is built against.

**④-a — "at that commit" versus "at or before" (the drafter's open choice; recommendation A was to leave it).** Leaving it as written is not right, because the record is not silent: bound line 3 says "green at the commit it snapshots", and "The full-battery reading" requires the stable lane's reader "against the snapshot's own commit". That reader (`release.yml:1551`; `scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs:797-830`) selects the newest completed `schedule` or `push` run of `CI` and `Lint & Type Check` whose head is the commit **or a first-parent ancestor within 400 commits** (`:864`), reports the distance (`:909`), and passes on "at or before" (`:1074`); push runs are affected-only (`:826-829`), and 62 of 100 recent `CI` push runs on main were cancelled (`:814-816`), so for a snapshot of HEAD the deciding run is routinely a few landings back and narrower than the schedule run. Two sentences in one record now carry two guarantees, and the approval screen will carry one of them. Either (i) say under bound line 3 that "at that commit" is read as the stable lane reads the version commit — the newest full-battery verdict at or before it on the first-parent chain — which is a reading of the ruling's words, not a new decision, and lets the maintainer see what "green" means on the prompt; or (ii) require the lane to snapshot the head of the newest green full-battery run (distance 0 — the reader already answers "at" exactly, so no new reader is needed, and the ruling holds literally). I would take (ii) for the lane and would accept (i) for the record; the record must not keep both. Should-fix (S3).

**④-b — a pointer callout under D1 (the drafter chose none).** Add it, under D1 **and D4**, in the 2026-09-29 house shape (ADR:61, :91: a blockquote "⚠️ Amended …" under the decision, not a rewrite of its text). D4's heading — "`workflow_dispatch` survives as the repair lane, with no version input" — is no longer a complete statement of what a dispatch may do, and a reader of D1 or D4 alone does not reach the Status line or the end of the file. The order's "D1–D6 text is not rewritten" is kept by a callout, as the precedent shows. Should-fix (S4).

**Fidelity attributions (S5, should-fix, wording only).** Mark the trial-start sentence and the D3 "removed in the same change" sentence as this record's readings (or cite 6664069140 for the first), so the next reader can tell the maintainer's lines from the seat's.

Must-fix: M1. Should-fix: S1, S2, S3 (④-a), S4 (④-b), S5. A re-render is owed on the head that carries them.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-30590-adr-0125-next-lane`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fb905387858b2789f7887522227e3019871a89cd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0125-release-approval-gate-replaces-the-typed-version.md + .github/workflows/release.yml, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs, scripts/release-dist-tags.mjs, scripts/release-publish.sh, scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs, scripts/sync-protocol-version.mjs, scripts/sync-template-versions.mjs, .changeset/config.json, package.json (the `version` script), AGENTS.md (Prime Directive #15), docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md, docs/releases-maintenance.md, packages/services/service-push/package.json, and the published `@changesets/cli@3.0.3` / `@changesets/apply-release-plan@8.1.1` / `@changesets/assemble-release-plan@7.0.0` sources (the versions `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins; read from the registry tarballs, nothing installed or run)

Round 4, the last check, of the independent full review on card #30590 (ADR-0125 amendment, #29466 ruling B). Round 1 on `28c6fc09` is record 6672362721 (FAIL: M1 + S1–S5); round 2 on `8adeb779` PASS with W1–W3; round 3 on `14115bea47` PASS with W2′ and W3a′. This head is one commit, `fb90538785` ("say publishing jobs throughout, drop a wrong parenthetical"), on `14115bea47`; `git diff 14115bea47..fb90538785` is four lines changed in the one ADR file; the delta against `origin/main` (`447226b222`, merge-base `ab44ec94b0`) is still that file alone, +69/−1, and against the round-1 head +21/−15. Every file cited in rounds 1 to 3 is byte-identical across `badf24dffc`, `ab44ec94b0`, `f0ad1f790c` and `447226b222`, so every earlier file:line citation still holds and is relied on below. Registry re-read at 2026-11-06T00:2xZ: `@objectstack/cli` `next` 18.2.0 / `latest` 18.3.0; `@objectstack/service-push` still E404. Check-runs on this head: 8 at the first read, 38 at the last with 13 in progress, 0 failures; CI is not awaited by this record (the round-1 head's 46 runs all finished green; rounds 2 to 4 change prose only, inside the same section and callout shapes). Judged against the tree, not against the drafter's account of it.

### ① Derived judgments

**Do W2′ and W3a′ close? Both do. Nothing new is false.**

- **W2′ — closed.** The D1 callout (line 63), the D4 callout (line 85) and the ⛔ bullet (line 226) now say "publishing jobs", matching the requirement "Dispatch-only, and exclusive" (line 212: "none of the stable lane's publishing jobs — `release-integrity`, the stable `full-battery` gate and `publish`"), and line 235 ("the `stale-prompts` job … untouched") is literally true: `stale-prompts` (`release.yml:1422`, PUSH LANE 3; `:1459-1461`) is left to run on a snapshot dispatch, mints nothing and cancels only push-lane prompts whose version is on npm (`release-pending-publish.mjs:170-185`). One sentence keeps the older shorthand: line 203, the D4 reading, "runs none of the stable lane's jobs (the exclusivity requirement below)". It points at the requirement that defines the set by name, so it is a shorthand with its definition attached rather than a fourth voice; a one-word edit ("publishing jobs") would make the file uniform, and nothing depends on it.
- **W3a′ — closed.** The parenthetical about the template syncs is dropped. What "Workspace only" still claims — the lane runs the bare `changeset version --snapshot next`, never `pnpm run version`, "whose chain aborts at `sync-protocol-version.mjs` on a major below 1" — is true: `package.json`'s `version` script chains `sync-protocol-version.mjs` and the later syncs with `&&` after `changeset version`, and `scripts/sync-protocol-version.mjs` exits 1 when the parsed major is not an integer of 1 or more, which `0.0.0-next-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` is not. The paragraph makes no claim about what the template syncs would do, so nothing in it can disagree with `sync-template-versions.mjs`.

**Carried from rounds 1 to 3, re-checked at this head — all still hold.** Every bound line of ruling 6663894403 is carried unsoftened (line 3 in the ruling's own words, read literally). The sentences that decide what the ruling left open are the four readings forced by the ruling's own lines — the commit choice (head of the newest green full-battery run, distance zero from the reader that exists), the debut rule, the pre-mode refusal, exclusivity — plus the two marked as this record's readings (trial start, cites 6664069140; removal with D1's reversion, with the relay reason, AGENTS.md:315-316). No sentence in this delta decides anything. Truth against the code at `447226b222`: the D1 and D4 callouts; `release.yml:182-184`, `:193-200`, `:208-227`, `:218-222`, `:959-961`, `:1459-1461`, `:1497-1551`, `:1564`, `:1568`, `:1586`, `:1608-1612`, `:1635-1637`, `:1657`, `:1977`, `:2030-2073`, `:269-271`, `:2081`; `release-publish.sh:98`, `:112`; `release-dist-tags.mjs:35-42`, `:51-53`; `release-pending-publish.mjs:174-176`, `:282`, `:381-387`; `scheduled-full-run.mjs:826-827`, `:864`, `:870-888`, `:892-915`, `:909`; `.changeset/config.json:10-121` (109 names, equal to the 109 non-private workspace manifests), `:52`, no `pre.json`; ADR-0087:335; `docs/releases-maintenance.md:191-201`; changesets `index.mjs:57`, `:62`, `version.mjs:38`, `:47-53`, `publish.mjs:19-24`, `:61-66`, `getPublishPlan.mjs:599-603`, `:605-650`, `:627-631`, `apply-release-plan:178-181`, `:288-292`, `:302-320`, `assemble-release-plan:197-210`, `:241-263`. The live debut case is unchanged: `@objectstack/service-push` public, in the fixed group, 18.2.0 in the tree, absent from npm. The round-1 inexactness inherited from the ruling's wording (changesets does not rewrite `workspace:*` ranges; `pnpm publish` substitutes them) is stated correctly in "The dry run".

### ② Semver level
